i.313600655:
Today, I completed the annual electrical system inspection. During my evaluation, I found that most of the baseboard outlets are ungrounded. Ungrounded receptacles are a safety concern, particularly when three-prong appliances or equipment are plugged into them. In the event of an electrical fault, an improperly grounded system can create a potential shock hazard by allowing energized metal components to become electrically charged.

I also observed that the main electrical panel is advanced in age. Due to the age of the equipment, replacement is recommended. Electrical panels and their internal safety components can deteriorate over time, and older circuit breakers may become less reliable and may fail to trip properly during an overload or fault condition. This can increase the risk of overheating and electrical damage.

Additionally, the building’s water piping system is not properly bonded/grounded. A properly sized grounding/bonding conductor should be installed from the main electrical service to the water piping system near the water meter. This provides a proper path for fault current and helps reduce the risk of electrical shock when using metal plumbing fixtures.

The customer advised that they will address the ungrounded receptacles. However, they requested an estimate for replacement of the main electrical panel and installation of the required water-piping grounding/bonding connection.

All available solutions were presented to the customer. An estimate for the requested work was provided separately.

i.316326921:
LPH arrived to begin the annual electrical system check. Upon arrival, Sabina reported two concerns/questions that she had for her electrical system. The first was her LED puck lights in her bedroom would flicker briefly every time she adjusted her ceiling fan speed. We informed Sabina that her LED lights are reading the harmonic interference, which is causing these lights to respond to that interference. Installing an electronic based control system instead of a mechanical will help alleviate the harmonic interference that she’s witnessing with these fixtures. She also informed us of a LED puck light that would struggle turn on sometimes and also flicker periodically when on. We informed Sabina that this fixture’s internal driver is failing and the entire fixture will need to be swapped out to remedy this. 

We began our evaluation at the main electrical/distribution panel. This is where we assessed the internal conditions, age, connections and voltage readings. During this inspection, all of the inspected parameters meet the required threshold for a healthy panel.

We discovered that there’s no system put in place to protect appliances/electronics from spikes of electric which target the sensitive components inside these units. A whole home surge protection device is recommended if the homeowners were interested in  protecting their main utility equipment with a one time investment unit.

Next, we inspected all of the protective systems for personnel and equipment in the home such as the smoke detectors, GFI protection devices, and the grounding system. First, we discovered that the water meter does meet today’s grounding standards to protect against any leakage of electricity from traveling on the pipes. The next was confirmation that all of the existing smoke detectors and carbon monoxide detectors are installed in the right locations and up-to-date. All other devices in the home were tested and functioning properly prior to leaving today.

We provided options to remedy all of our electrical recommendations, which was presented today. All of the options that were not approved will be emailed along with the electrical evaluation form and invoice for today’s visit. We thank you for allowing us in your home to service you and we look forward to servicing you in the future.

i.326469032:
Today, I completed the annual electrical system inspection. During my evaluation, I found the main electrical panel to be zinsco panel. Zinsco panels were recalled in the early 1980s due to known fire hazards associated with the breakers failing to trip properly. When breakers do not trip as designed, excessive heat can build up in the breakers, wiring, and connected equipment, creating a potential fire hazard.

Due to the age and safety concerns associated with this panel, replacement of the main electrical panel is strongly recommended. These panels are considered unsafe, and replacement breakers and components may no longer be readily available if an existing breaker fails.

I also found several three-prong receptacles that are not properly grounded. Ungrounded three-prong outlets do not provide the intended equipment-grounding protection and can present a safety hazard. In the event of an electrical fault, exposed metal components or equipment could potentially become energized. The homeowner said he will adress the outlets.

I recommend replacing the existing two-prong and ungrounded receptacles with properly installed GFCI-protected receptacles, as applicable, to improve safety and bring the electrical system into compliance with current requirements where permitted.

The exterior electrical service is approximately 30 years old or older. I did not observe any immediate issues with the exterior service during today’s inspection. I did advise the homeowner that if the complete electrical service is replaced, a 10-year warranty would be provided. If only the necessary repairs are performed without replacing the complete service, the warranty would be limited to one year.

A customer-supplied thermostat was also installed. All available solutions were presented to the homeowner, including the option to have a thermostat installed inside. Because the thermostat was supplied by the customer, the thermostat itself is not covered under our warranty. A one-year labor warranty applies.

The invoice has been emailed to the customer.

i.331406411:
This afternoon I arrived at the Ternoski family home to conduct their annual electrical system and safety check. Upon my arrival, Mr. Ternoski informed me that they had accidentally overloaded the circuit which they are using to supply power to their RV. Upon performing a thorough evaluation of the circuit I do un there to be no tripped breakers, and all breaker were providing 120v of power (at minimum), yet no power was reaching the garage. I began to conduct a very thorough analysis of all devices, both known and unknown, that could potentially be on this circuit. I found no discrepancies. From there I entered the homes crawl space which spans the homes entire footprint minus the garage. I located the entry from most of the homes circuits to the breaker panel and found several discrepancies. I found improper and unsafe Junctioning means, including open junctions and splices, improperly located and unweatherized “in-wall” splices free hanging. More concerning yet, I noted that the homes dryer vent is vented almost directly onto these improper junctions. What this has done is created a thick film of dryer lint on these already potentially hazardous junctions. I have included photos of my findings, and provided an option to essentially dismantle, and properly reinstall all of these non code-compliant splices. 

Circling back to the loss of power, after digging through several of the junctions, I identified one bundle of wires which had too many hot wires under one wire nut. It appeared that one wire had been worked loose of the wire nut, and potentially further loosened during our overload event. I retracted this circuit and worked out which wires were live from the bundle in order to separate the cluster of wires properly using appropriately sized wire nuts. I was able to restore power to the garage, and also identified that the garage was being powered by a breaker labeled as “master bedroom”.

Finally I provided an estimate to run an appropriate dedicated 30A circuit and plug for the RV, as to avoid potential overloads down the road. 

If you have any questions, concerns, or if you would like to move forward with any of today’s provided estimates, please do not hesitate to reach out. Thank you for your patience today, and I look forward to our next visit!

Today, I completed the annual electrical system inspection. Upon evaluation, the main electrical panel was found to be in good condition. There were no signs of rust or corrosion, all electrical connections were tight, and there were no indications of overheating at the breakers.

All other electrical components throughout the home were tested and were found to be functioning properly.

However, I did identify an issue with the home’s grounding and bonding system. The grounding system consists of two primary components: the grounding electrode system (ground rods) and the bonding of the home’s metal water and gas piping.

The required bonding connection from the main electrical panel to the water piping is currently missing. A properly sized copper bonding conductor should be installed from the main electrical panel to the appropriate locations on the water piping, including the house and street sides of the water meter, with the gas piping properly bonded as required.

Proper bonding helps ensure that metal piping, gas appliances, water fixtures, and other conductive components throughout the home remain at the same electrical potential and provides a safe path for fault current back to the electrical system.

As the system currently stands, there is a potential shock hazard in the event of an electrical fault involving the gas piping, water piping, appliances, or other metal components.

Recommended Solution

Provide and install the required bonding connections to properly bond the home’s water and gas piping to the electrical grounding system and bring the system into proper compliance.

A proposal/invoice for the recommended bonding work has been provided by email for review.

i.338676000:
Out to home today for the yearly plumbing system check. Upon arrival to home, there were two main concerns. Home is experiencing backups and slow drainage from the laundry, shower, and lavatory sink in the basement of the home. Upon inspection, identified that the issue is relating to improper venting and slow buildup. Confirmed the issue is not relating to the main drain. The toilet in the downstairs bathroom, floor drain, and kitchen sink are all working properly at this time. Suggested best solution is to install a mechanical air vent and perform a drain cleaning service for branch lines. The next concern has to do with the main water shut off valve. Homeowner states the current main valve is not very accessible and is requesting pricing on relocating the valves. Upon inspection of valves, confirmed the valves are old and unreliable. Suggested replacement of main shut off valves and relocating the secondary valve to an accessible location in the utility room. 

From there, performed the full home plumbing inspection. Performed flush of water heater system. Tested water pressure to be within a safe threshold for inside the home. Performed water quality test and found high hardness and chlorine in the water. Suggested corrective measures for water quality to protect the home, plumbing, and occupants of the home. 

Found several other concerns during visit today. In the utility room, identified the laundry faucet is leaking down through sink on concrete floor. Kitchen faucet upstairs is loose and in poor condition. Also in the upstairs bathroom, the tub spout is faulty and not diverting the water properly.

Went over all suggestions and recommendations based on the plumbing inspection today. Homeowner approved the drain rebuild and drain cleaning service today. Scheduled to return Tuesday October 6th first stop to complete requested services and repairs. Collected a 30% deposit for work to be completed. Remainder of balance to be collected upon completion of services. All other pricing provided today is valid for 60 days. Thank you for trusting LPH.

e.341753298: During inspection, found the laundry faucet leaking down behind the utility tub sink. Also observed no valves installed for faucet. This solution includes replacement of laundry faucet and installation of new hot and cold shut off valves.
e.341753356:
During inspection, performed water quality test and found high hardness and chlorine in the water. The major contaminents work together to cause plumbing issues longterm due to scale build up and rubber deterioration. With the installation of a water treatment system, water inside the home will be filtered of hardness and chlorine improving water quality inside the home. 

This solution includes full installation of our CitySoft unit inside the utility room. 
*If an electrical outlet is needed, additional charges may apply.
e.341774546: In the upstairs bathroom, found that the diverter tub spout does not fully function properly allowing half the water to flow out the spout when the shower is in use. This solution includes installation of new chrome tub spout.
e.341775680: In the upstairs kitchen, found the faucet to be loose and the sprayer head to be broken. With the faucet being loose, this is allowing water to leak down into the cabinet. This solution includes installation of new kitchen faucet with a similar style pull-out spray faucet from moen.

Today, I arrived at the Themis residence to perform a complimentary electrical system check. Upon arrival, the homeowner informed me of several electrical concerns she wanted me to evaluate, including an issue with the dryer and a dining room light that was not functioning properly.

Upon evaluating the dryer, I found that the dryer itself appears to have an internal failure or a failed component, which is causing it not to operate properly. The issue does not appear to be related to the home’s electrical supply.

The homeowner also reported that the dining room light had stopped working after she reset the breaker. I proceeded to the electrical panel to inspect the breakers, voltages, and connections. Upon inspection, I found that both 200-amp main electrical panels are enclosed within a cabinet and are currently inaccessible because they are completely stuck within the cabinet.

The two main electrical panels are original to the home and are over 35 years old. Due to their age, there is an increased likelihood of breaker and other component failures, which can contribute to electrical distribution problems and potential safety concerns. The panels are Sylvania panels, which are known to have issues with breakers failing to trip properly under certain fault conditions. A breaker that fails to trip when required can allow excessive current to continue flowing, potentially resulting in overheating or damage to connected electrical components.

Based on the age, condition, accessibility, and manufacturer of the existing equipment, I informed homeowner both 200-amp main electrical panels need to be replaced to improve electrical safety, reliability, and proper power distribution throughout the home.

I also explained that the existing cabinet will need to be modified or removed as necessary to provide proper access when the panels are replaced. In addition, surge protection will need to be installed at the main panels as part of the panel replacement to meet current code requirements. Themis didn’t want anything els checked during today visit.

An estimate/solution was presented to the homeowner. She stated that she would discuss the recommended work with her daughter and get back to us regarding how she would like to proceed. 
Thank you for letting us ensure safety to your home.

Technician performed water quality testing and found the home’s water hardness to be 5 grains per gallon (GPG) and the chlorine level to be . 5 ppm. A hardness level of 5 GPG is considered hard water and can lead to calcium and magnesium scale buildup inside water heaters, plumbing fixtures, faucets, shower heads , and water-using appliances. Over time, this mineral buildup can reduce appliance efficiency, shorten equipment life expectancy, cause spotting on dishes and glassware, and leave soap residue on fixtures and surfaces. The presence of chlorine, while common in municipal water supplies, can contribute to dry skin and hair and may deteriorate rubber seals and gaskets within the plumbing system over time.

To improve water quality and help protect the home’s plumbing system, technician recommends installing a City Soft water treatment system. The system is designed to soften the water by removing the hardness minerals that cause scale buildup while also reducing chlorine levels throughout the home. Benefits of the system include improved soap and detergent performance, reduced spotting and scaling, softer-feeling water, and increased protection and efficiency of plumbing fixtures and water-using appliances.

The proposed installation location for the City Soft system is near the existing water heater. The water softener inlet would come from the water meter approximately 20’ away. The softener’s backwash drain lines will be routed and connected to the existing main drain located near the water meter. The system also requires a dedicated electrical outlet for operation and regeneration cycles. The home’s electrical panel is located approximately 20 feet away, and an outlet will need to be installed and provided at the equipment location prior to or as part of the installation. Once installed, the system will provide conditioned water to the entire home and help minimize the long-term effects of hard water and chlorine exposure on the plumbing system.

i.341685691:
This estimate includes having Lancaster Plumbing and Heating make a warranty repair on the water softener. It would include removal of the mechanical parts of the head that control the stages of the water softeners regeneration. This repair is covered under both the manufacturer’s parts warranty and Lancaster Plumbing and Heating’s labor warranty.

We came out today to take a look at the water softener because it was showing an error code. The error code was indicating that there was a motor failure. This usually means that during regeneration the computer was telling the spacer stack assembly to switch positions and it took too long or got stuck.

The technician began diagnosing the issue by disconnecting power and trying a hard reset of the electrical components. This did not fix the issue, so the technician provided an estimate to perform a warranty repair. The warranty repair included replacing the spacer stack assembly, and the motor that drives the functions for the spacer stack assembly. Once the repair was completed, the technician put the water softener through an abbreviated regeneration twice in order to verify that the system was now working properly. Both attempts on the abbreviated regeneration were successful and everything was in proper operation at this time.

The technician did discover a secondary issue, but it had to do with the Brian tank. The homeowners have been using salt pellets instead of salt crystals, and this is caused bridging within the brine tank. The technician suggested that the salt be dug out of the brine tank in order to fix this issue. Moving forward we did recommend the use of salt crystals because they do dissolve easier with these particular systems.

If you have any other questions or concerns that arise after today’s visit, please do not hesitate to give us a call. Thank you for continuing to trust Lancaster Plumbing and Heating with all of your home service needs. 
This estimate includes having Lancaster Plumbing and Heating unload the brine tank in order to remove a large chunk of salt pellets.

Technician tested the electrical outlet supplying the heat tape and verified that the outlet is properly grounded and operating correctly. During the inspection, Technician observed that the water main is currently wrapped with approximately 1/8-inch-thick Seal Seal foam insulation, which is typically used for foundation applications. This insulation provides minimal protection against freezing temperatures.

Technician recommends replacing the existing insulation on the water main with 1/2-inch to 1-inch-thick pipe insulation to provide additional protection from freezing temperatures. Approximately 25 feet of insulation would be required to properly insulate the exposed water main.

Technician also recommends insulating the pit where the water main enters the mobile home from below grade. Regular R-19 insulation should be installed around the pit to help retain heat and provide additional protection for the water main during freezing temperatures.

Technician also recommends replacing the existing pressure tank and tank tee assembly. The new tank assembly would include a 40/60 pressure switch, pressure gauge, pressure relief valve, and drain-down valve. Replacing these components at the same time will provide a complete upgrade of the well system’s pumping and pressure-control components.

Date: 10/8 9-4
Contact: 4174 Dispatch Fee: $49

i.342862190:
Technician investigated concerns of sewer gas odor entering the main-floor master bathroom shower area and laundry room. Technician checked the water level in the master bathroom shower drain and inspected the 3” vent termination through the roof, which is located directly above the master bathroom. The 3” vent was found to extend approximately 6–8” above the roof.

Technician explained that windy conditions can create a Venturi effect at the vent termination, potentially drawing air through the vent system and affecting the water seal in the shower P-trap. Wind can also create direct downdrafts through the vent, which may contribute to sewer gas odors entering the home. Technician discussed raising the existing vent termination and adding a U-bend configuration using two 3” 90° fittings to help reduce the potential for wind-driven downdrafts.

Technician also recommended installing a 2” Trap Guard in the shower drain. The Trap Guard allows water to drain normally while providing an additional barrier to help prevent sewer gas from entering the home if the P-trap water seal is compromised.

The main-floor laundry room is equipped with two laundry drains, each with a 2” P-trap. One of the drains is not regularly used, and the water in the P-trap may be evaporating and allowing sewer gas to enter the laundry room. The unused drain will either be used for the dehumidifier discharge to maintain the P-trap water seal or capped to prevent sewer gas from entering through the drain.

The homeowner plans to purchase a trap guard before addressing the vent through the roof.

i.343560853: Tech arrived and found a four flash code on the smart screen on the Water heater. It is an electric water heater prestige model. That code states that the unit shut itself off due to how high the temperature was getting. Tech found that the thermostat was tripped. Tech reset thermostat and the code still read. Tech then checked voltage and continuity to the elements and found both to be where they should be. Tech then disconnected the wires going to the smart screen then plugged it back in. The code went away at this time. Tech called tech support to find out the underlying problem. Tech explained everything to tech support, tech support stated that there is no active code so they cannot help. Tech was unable to figure out why the thermostat tripped. When tech was putting everything together the unit kept shutting off due to it sensing water. Tech verified that there is nothing wet touching the unit. Currently there is a solid red light indicating that the sensor is wet. Tech sees rust on the unit and believes that the unit could be leaking from the tank ever so slightly. Homeowner stated that the frequently have to go to the unit and Manuel open the valve that shuts the unit off. As of now homeowner has hot water, tech made sure to stay to ensure water got hot. Tech found it very peculiar that the water heater was rusting at such a young age. Homeowner is on a well, so technician wanted to check the acidity in the water. Technician found that the water is acidic and it is at 6. You want it around seven because that is neutral. Technician left a quote to install an acid neutralizer. Homeowners have to discuss financing and then reach out to Lph. Thank you for trusting Lph.

e.343704705: Tech saw that the water heater is 4y old and is already starting to rust. Tech wanted to check water quality to see if that’s the main issue. Tech found the PH at 6. e.343705424:
The homeowner would like to install a new toilet in the main floor laundry room. To complete the installation, the technician will modify the existing drain and water supply piping.

The technician will repipe the existing 3-inch PVC main drain in the basement by extending it to the new toilet location on the left side of the laundry tub. The existing laundry drain will then be reconnected to the newly installed 3-inch main drain to maintain proper drainage for both fixtures.

After the drain modifications are complete, the technician will shut off the home’s main water supply and extend the cold water line to the new toilet location. Once the drain and water supply have been roughed in, the new toilet can be installed, connected, and tested to verify proper operation and to ensure there are no leaks.

Technician would connect the front outside hose bib to the cold water main.
